source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Carrollton campus publishes 45 MW of IT load capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this corresponds to roughly 1,125 racks. At 8 H100-equivalent accelerators per rack, a common configuration, that scales to approximately 9,000 accelerators, assuming the full IT load is deployed to GPU compute and not mixed with other workloads. The campus certifications qualify it for PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISAA, ISO 27001, and SSAE 16 Type II compliance workloads, and it meets TIA-942 Tier standards for data center design.

Within Texas, this campus ranks third by published capacity. Texas shows 19 facilities with published megawatt figures totaling 475 MW across the operators who have disclosed specifications to public spec pages. CyrusOne Carrollton therefore represents 9.5% of the state's published IT capacity. The state has 133 mapped facilities in total, the majority of which do not publish capacity figures.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on dispatch. The 45 MW figure is published as IT load capacity, not as currently deployed or committed to AI workloads. The fact that the facility meets compliance certifications suggests readiness for regulated workloads, but does not indicate accelerator density or current tenant mix. The power and space exist to host substantial GPU clusters if deployed at that density, but the operator's spec page does not state how much of this capacity is allocated to AI training versus other uses.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
